verdict.rationale: Floot documents an assistant that takes delegated build tasks: you describe an integration and the endpoints, tables, and screens get built; you can point at elements or annotate screenshots for it to pick up; and you can ask it to restore checkpoints. However, much of the 'your AI' material describes external assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) driving Floot over MCP rather than an assistant built into the product, so in-product coverage is only partly evidenced. missing for 10: clear first-party documentation that the assistant is native to the Floot editor rather than an external MCP client, detail on the range and autonomy of delegable tasks, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: point at an element or annotate a screenshot for the assistant to pick up
Describe the integration you want to your AI assistant, and the endpoints, database tables, and screens get built for you.
Ask it to restore a checkpoint from before the change went sideways.
Floot turns a plain-language description into a real, deployed full-stack app
